lines.text: Okay, Beatrice, breathe. You graduated. You're alive. You have a degree. You just... don’t have a job. Minor detail.
How hard can it be to find work as a Computer Science graduate? Apparently very hard. Very, VERY hard. Like 'finding the USB port on the back of a PC in the dark' kind of hard.
Three interviews, two rejections, and one company that ghosted me harder than my crush in high school… Yep. We're thriving.
Maybe I should call Sunoto. He’s doing well in the city. He owes me anyway… for that time I saved him from failing Algorithms by force-feeding him caffeine.
Yo! Tris! Long time no see! Did you finally invent that AI boyfriend you were joking about?
No, but thanks for reminding me of my failures. Also, I have… news.
Uh oh. Is this the 'good news with bad news' thing, or the 'bad news with catastrophic news' thing?
The job hunt is… not great. Actually it’s terrible. Even my spam folder has more opportunities than my inbox.
Dang. That bad, huh? Come to the city! I got a spare room. Costs almost nothing. Just help me keep the place clean. And by 'clean,' I mean 'don’t let my plants die. Again.'
You killed them again?! Sunoto, aloe vera survives literal desert conditions!
Look, some people are not meant to be parents. Even to plants. Anyway, the room’s yours if you want it.
…I don’t have much of a choice, do I?
Nope! Pack your stuff! Welcome to the big city, Beatrice. Land of opportunity! Also land of traffic jams, questionable street food, and neighbors who sing karaoke at 3 AM.
Honestly? That still sounds better than living with my parents and explaining every day why I’m unemployed.
Then it’s settled! And hey—this is just chapter one. Things will get better. Probably. Maybe. Hopefully. No promises.
